title: Prime-abundant numbers enumerated without sieving, to 10^13
description:
The prime-abundant numbers — the n with rad(n) dividing σ(n), OEIS A175200 — are listed without sieving. The defining condition, read backwards, forces every prime of n to divide σ(qa) for another prime power of n: no prime of n is free, so all of them appear inside factorisations that have to be computed anyway.

This reaches 1013 with 85,695 terms, where the published b-file stops at 7,271,402,112 with 10,000 terms, and extends the counts of prime-perfect numbers from 109 to 1013. The counts at 109 reproduce exactly the two values published by Pollack and Pomerance (INTEGERS 12A, 2012): 198 prime-perfect and 5,328 prime-abundant.

Also included: three elementary theorems (unique factorisation into weakly connected atoms, which turns out to be trivial for 99.9% of elements below 1010; infinitude with an O(1) certificate; and a closed formula that counts the two-prime elements without searching for them), and a body of negative results — six candidate invariants that do not predict the size of these sets, measured across 30 local multiplicative functions, each ruled out against a criterion fixed in advance.

Verification: identical sets against an independent segmented sieve to 1010, identical to the OEIS b-file term by term, and 0 false positives in 207,284 individually re-verified terms. verify.py reruns 38 checks in seconds with no dependencies.
